A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MS-Diffusion. All 22 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable and support matching the methods, equations, tables, and figures despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original MS-Diffusion results on DreamBench and MS-Bench in Table 2, numerical ablations in Table 3, and generated examples and analyses throughout the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds qualitative baseline comparisons, diagnostic examples, and an experiment using pseudo layout guidance.

M1.justification: The core architecture, training objective, grounding resampler, and multi-subject attention remain unchanged. Appendix M adds a tested inference variant that thresholds text attention maps into layout masks after T denoising steps, using either rough boxes or no layout guidance beforehand.

E1.justification: The training corpus, DreamBench, and MS-Bench coverage remain unchanged. v2 adds limited qualitative coverage of human identity and anime references, mixed human/anime compositions, and more complex interaction prompts, including holding, playing, and spatial relationships (Figures 17–18).

E2.justification: Appendix F adds actual multi-subject comparisons with Mix-of-Show, Cones2, and Break-A-Scene (Figures 8–9), substantially extending comparison coverage to tuning-based approaches. The original comparator sets in Table 2 and Figures 4–5 remain intact.

E3.justification: Appendix M introduces a new inference experiment comparing pseudo layout masks with and without an initial rough-box prior. Existing benchmark metrics, sample counts, training budgets, and guidance settings remain unchanged; the added statement about qualitative results using no benchmark fine-tuning is a disclosure rather than an established protocol revision.

E4.justification: v2 adds qualitative module-ablation evidence (Figure 6), examines detail preservation on uncommon subjects (Figure 13), probes complex interactions (Figure 17), and tests dependence on explicit layout input (Figure 11). These substantially expand the diagnostic evidence beyond the retained numerical ablations, layout tests, attribution analysis, and interpolation examples.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five generated images per evaluation sample in Appendix C. Neither reports new seeds, repeated training-run counts, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 2–3 remain identical. v2 substantially expands qualitative outcomes through tuning-based comparisons, uncommon-subject failures, interaction and human/anime examples, and reduced subject consistency without an initial layout prior; it also replaces some Figure 4 examples. These additions do not establish higher benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same mathematical substance, and neither version introduces theoretical results or proofs. v2 makes transposes explicit in standard attention expressions, clarifying notation without changing the underlying mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about zero-shot multi-subject personalization, grounding resampling, layout-guided attention, frozen base-model parameters, and image/text fidelity. Added supporting experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation and applicability discussion: Appendix D attributes uncommon-subject detail loss to the CLIP encoder; Appendix F discusses tuning-based overfitting and interaction failures; Appendix I links interaction handling to the preserved base model. Appendix M qualifies explicit-layout dependence through pseudo guidance while acknowledging reduced subject consistency.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies the image encoder as CLIP and clarifies that qualitative MS-Diffusion results use no benchmark fine-tuning. It also partially documents pseudo-layout inference, although threshold and T values are unspecified. Existing software versions, hardware, training hyperparameters, and project access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Section 3.2 and Appendix F substantially broaden positioning against tuning-based multi-concept methods and approaches modifying text cross-attention, adding discussion of Mix-of-Show, Cones2, Break-A-Scene, Subject-Diffusion, and FastComposer. Section 3.1 also attributes decoupled image/text attention to IP-Adapter instead of Stable Diffusion.

P1.justification: v2 adds a discussion subsection and several appendix sections, makes local explanatory edits, updates affiliations and publication headers, and switches to author-year citations. Most original prose and the main narrative sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands visual presentation with new multi-panel ablations, tuning-based comparisons, pseudo-layout tests, uncommon-subject diagnostics, and interaction/human/anime examples. It also revises comparison-panel styling and adopts the ICLR layout; existing construction, attribution, ControlNet, and interpolation figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added tuning-based comparisons, diagnostic examples, and discussion of encoder and layout limitations provide useful support and clarify applicability. The improvement is limited: the benchmark and ablation numbers remain unchanged, the additional evidence is qualitative, and the pseudo-layout procedure omits threshold and switching-step values needed for reproduction.
